messages:
Maya (product): Heads up — ACME legal sent a draft today asking for contract-level SLOs we don’t currently guarantee: 99.95% uptime, p95 inference latency <200ms for their primary model, and 24/7 Sev1 support with 30m response. They want a February 1 go-live window. Can we triage and route?
Li (sales): Context: ACME is on a growth plan, likely >$250k ARR if we can hit these terms. They're willing to pay for Dedicated or a premium support addon. Their PM wants firm SLAs in the MSA. Timeline is tight.
Sam (support): Noted. Current premium support (Gold) has 12h business response and no guaranteed latency SLOs. We can offer 24/7 on-call as an add-on but need runbook + escalation path.
Andrew (eng-sre): Key questions: what model & qps profile? Any spikes (batching) or steady stream? Also need to know acceptable fallback behavior if we miss latency (degraded model, cached responses).
Maya (product): From ACME: primary model is text-gen-xl-7b, expected steady 35 req/s peak 80 req/s, 40 tokens avg. They want hard p95 <200ms regionally in us-west. Fallback allowed to a slightly smaller variant (xl-6b-quant) but only if accuracy drop <3% per their eval set.
Jess (customer-success): ACME is okay with a canary + waitlist approach, but legal insists SLA terms in MSA before prod rollout. They will accept a phased SLA: beta (monitoring + monthly reporting) -> guaranteed SLA after Dedicated capacity validation.
Sam (support): Proposal for triage: 1) Create product backlog ticket for SLA delivery (SLA-ACME-175000). 2) Define acceptance criteria + runbook. 3) Confirm billing + dedicated capacity order. 4) Add 24/7 escalation on-call rotation and paging policy.
Andrew (eng-sre): I sketched required telemetry/monitoring: 
```
- p95/p99 latency metrics per region/model
- uptime (service+model) derived from health checks
- request tracing id for each customer request
- auto-escalation hook when p95 > target for 3 consecutive 5m windows
```
Will need ~3 GPUs reserved in us-west for peak plus 30% buffer. Estimating cost/back-of-envelope: $Xk/mo.
Li (sales): If Dedicated is needed, we can attach capacity fees to the contract. Sales/legal want clear launch criteria we can present to customer.
Maya (product): Draft of launch/acceptance criteria (for product backlog):
```
- 99.95% measured monthly uptime for primary endpoint (per-region)
- p95 inference latency <200ms in us-west (measured over 1m windows) for 30 days in staging with prod-like load
- Automated alerting + pager on-call when p95 > 220ms for 10m
- Fallback behavior validated: model switch preserves <3% accuracy delta per ACME eval set
- Support: 24/7 pager with initial response <=30m and SOC handoff playbook
- Billing: Dedicated capacity reserved and invoiced before SLA enforcement
```
Maya (product): Owners: Product (Maya) to draft backlog epic + acceptance, Eng-SRE (Andrew) to scope infra and runbook, Support (Sam) to own pager & handoff, Sales (Li) to finalize contract language, CS (Jess) to coordinate eval set and rollout plan.
Andrew (eng-sre): I'll open infra ticket and include perf test harness targetting their qps/latency. Need access to ACME eval suite + sample traffic profile.
Jess (customer-success): I'll request the eval set from ACME today and ask for a synthetic traffic trace. Also confirm their tolerance for fallback during canary.
Li (sales): I'll draft the MSA clause and flag legal; will propose phased SLA language reflecting beta -> guaranteed SLA.
Sam (support): I'll prepare a one-pager runbook draft and an on-call schedule proposal. Paging integration with PagerDuty already exists; just need escalation TTLs.
incident-bot: Runbook created: /runbooks/sla-acme-175000. Action required: Product to attach acceptance criteria and Eng-SRE to populate monitoring alerts.
Maya (product): Next steps: I'll create the backlog epic SLA-ACME-175000, invite all owners to kickoff tomorrow 10am PT. If anyone can't make it, ping here with constraints. :thumbsup:
Li (sales): On my calendar.
Andrew (eng-sre): I'll be there.
Sam (support): 👍
Jess (customer-success): See you.
Maya (product): Thanks team — this will be the template if future customers ask for contract-level SLOs, we should capture any gaps during the epic and propose platform-level features to avoid bespoke work each time.
